title: TAPPaaS Module Catalog Schema
description:
Field schema for module-catalog.json — the per-repository module registry (renamed from modules.json, #305). Every 'managed: full' repository carries one, and `repository validate-catalog` checks it against this schema (#463).

A catalogue answers two questions and no others: WHERE is a module in this repository (moduleJson, found by moduleName or a legacyName it used to have), and WHICH VMID block is taken. Everything else about a module — tier, source, status, version, description — is read from the module's own JSON and is never restated here, because two copies of one fact drift (they had, by #463). The single exception is `stack`, repeated so a listing can group without opening every module file; the check reports a disagreement.

`stack` also says what a module IS: `foundation` a foundation module, `template` a template to copy rather than install (a Proxmox VM template, the module skeleton), `test` a fixture the suites install. Any other value, or none, is an application module — so an author unsure where a module belongs leaves it out and nothing breaks.

source.description: Where the modules in THIS repository come from (ADR-007b), stated once for the repository instead of on every entry — which is how the pre-#463 shape carried it. A module whose own JSON declares a `source` overrides it; a repository that states none is not official. Read by lib/ts/src/kind.ts, which defaults a non-official module with no authored `kind` to `vm`.

modules.description: Every module this repository ships, in one list (#463). The shape before it split these across foundationModules / applicationModules / proxmoxTemplates / testModules with `tier` on each entry; readers accept that for one stable cycle, and this schema still permits it below.

foundationModules.description: DEPRECATED (#463) — the pre-flat shape, still read for a stable cycle. A repository on it should move its entries into `modules`, where `stack: foundation` says what this list said.

applicationModules.description: DEPRECATED (#463) — the pre-flat shape. In `modules`, an application module is any entry whose stack is not foundation, template or test.

moduleName.description: The name this module is looked up by — the module's own directory name (ADR-026 D6.2).

legacyName.description: A name this module used to have, still matched by the resolver (firewall → network). Written when a module is renamed (scripts/move-module.sh --rename). Not in the module's own JSON: it is the repository's memory, not the module's.

moduleJson.description: Path to the module's JSON, relative to the repository root. The answer the catalogue exists to give.

vmid.description: The VMID block this module reserves — a DELIBERATE duplication of the module's own vmid, documented as such: picking a free block, or finding a collision, must not mean opening every module JSON in every repository. Omitted by a module with no guest of its own (a machine, an application). The check reports a disagreement with the module's JSON, and any two entries sharing one.

stack.description: The group this module belongs to — repeated from the module's own `stack` so a listing can group without opening every module file, and checked against it. `foundation`, `template` and `test` are reserved and say what the module is; any other value, or none, is an application module.

legacyEntry.description: An entry in the pre-#463 shape. Permitted so a repository that has not migrated still validates; `tier`, `source`, `status`, `category` and `repo` are the restatements the flat shape drops.
